mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 5.0% signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates for equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.5, or the mean return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits above 1.8 million units signals strong household demand and confidence, which drives corporate revenue expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative or flat 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1800.0, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 113.0 indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which signals deteriorating corporate earnings momentum and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 113.0, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in both personal consumption expenditures and residential investment signals strong aggregate demand, which increases corporate revenue visibility and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of GDPC1 and HOUST growth fails to produce positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative or insignificant coefficient (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 203.5) and a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 5.0) indicates a persistent inflationary environment with restrictive policy, which increases real interest rate expectations and suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both CPIAUCSL > 203.5 and FEDFUNDS > 5.0, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in employment (PAYEMS > 135,000) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE < 4.8) signals a strong labor market recovery, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates negative or flat 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 135000 and UNRATE < 4.8, or the interaction term in a predictive model is not positive and significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) combined with rising housing starts (HOUST > 1790) indicates robust household demand and confidence, which drives corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 368000 and HOUST > 1790.0, or the joint signal fails to outperform a baseline return (t-test p > 0.05).
